jobs.title: Principal Biomedical Engineer
jobs.description:
We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on - 30 Nov 2026

At MiniMed, you can begin a lifelong career of exploration and innovation, while helping make a difference in the lives of people living with diabetes around the globe. You'll lead with purpose, breaking down barriers to innovation for a more connected, compassionate world.

About The Role

MiniMed is seeking an experienced Principal Engineer to join our Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) Sensor R&D team. This role will provide technical leadership in the development, and improvement of next-generation CGM sensor technologies.

You will be working in our Northridge office 3 days in office/2 days remote.

In this role, you will lead complex technical investigations, develop and execute data-driven experimental strategies to characterize component- and system-level performance, and translate technical insights into actionable improvements that influence the design and reliability of next-generation Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) sensors. The role emphasizes structured problem-solving methodologies, including DMAIC, and the application of Design for Reliability and Manufacturability (DRM) principles to drive product robustness, performance, and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate will bring a strong background in medical device product development, preferably with expertise in electrochemical sensors and related medical device technologies. The candidate should demonstrate exceptional technical problem-solving and analytical capabilities, proven cross-functional leadership, and experience driving product improvements through systematic root cause investigations and Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) processes.

A Day in the Life

Responsibilities may include the following and other duties may be assigned:

Lead complex technical investigations across all phases of product development, including post-market performance, to identify root causes, characterize failure mechanisms, and drive product improvements.
Develop and implement advanced tools, methodologies, and structured problem-solving approaches (DMAIC) to address complex component- and system-level technical challenges.
Troubleshoot and characterize performance anomalies in microfabricated electrochemical biosensors through systematic experimentation, advanced analytical techniques, and data-driven analysis.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including Design, Manufacturing, Quality, and Regulatory, to develop and implement effective technical solutions that enhance product performance and reliability.
Design, develop, and optimize test methods, measurement techniques, and fixtures to improve product characterization, diagnostic capabilities, and testing efficiency.
Develop and execute verification, validation, and reliability test strategies to assess product performance, design robustness, and long-term reliability.
Conduct hands-on laboratory investigations, interpret experimental findings, and translate technical insights into actionable design recommendations and corrective actions.
Prepare and maintain technical documentation, including experimental protocols, investigation reports, test methods, and engineering assessments.
Evaluate product designs against performance specifications, regulatory requirements, and applicable national and international standards.
Support sustaining engineering and continuous improvement initiatives through technical impact assessments, risk evaluations, design reviews, and Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) processes.

Must Have: Minimum Requirements

Education and Experience:
Bachelor’s degree in biomedical engineering, chemical engineering or related engineering field with at least 7 years of experience in Medical Device, or an advanced degree with at least 5 years of experience in Medical Device.

Medical Device product development:
Demonstrated experience developing electrochemical medical devices within design controls and Quality Management systems; familiarity with FSA requirements, ISO 13485, risk analysis and FMEA.

Failure Analysis & Problem Solving:
Demonstrated experience in leading complex, cross-functional failure analysis investigations using structured problem-solving methodologies such as DMAIC, root cause analysis, fault-tree analysis, and hypothesis-driven experimentation.

Technical leadership:
Proven ability to lead complex projects with limited oversight, manage multiple priorities, influence cross-functional stakeholders, and coach or mentor engineers in structured problem-solving and failure analysis.

#BetterDaysStartNow

Nice to Have

Experience in electrochemical sensor design and development in an R&D environment
Experience leading complex root-cause investigations within medical device industry
Direct experience in characterization, design of experiments and data analysis methodologies (T-test, ANOVA and significance testing at a minimum)
Working knowledge of in-vitro and in-vivo testing of subcutaneous medical devices
Certification in DMAIC or equivalent Scientific Method problem solving for root cause analysis
Experience with statistical analysis of data (Ex. Minitab, JMP, Matlab, etc.)
Capable of working on multiple projects in a deadline driven environment
Greenbelt in DRM, Six Sigma
Cleanroom procedural experience

Physical Job Requirements

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this position, but they are not an exhaustive list of all the required responsibilities and skills of this position.

The physical demands described within the Responsibilities section of this job description are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. For Office Roles: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to be independently mobile. The employee is also required to interact with a computer and communicate with peers and co-workers. Contact your manager or local HR to understand the Work Conditions and Physical requirements that may be specific to each role.

Benefits & Compensation

MiniMed offers a competitive salary and flexible benefits package

At MiniMed, we put people first. A commitment to our employees lives at the core of our values: We recognize their contributions. They share in the success they help create. We offer a wide range of benefits, resources, and competitive compensation plans designed to support you at every stage of your career and life.

Salary ranges for U.S (excl. PR) locations (USD):$109,000.00 - $185,000.00

For roles located in California, Seattle WA, Washington DC, Boston MA, and New York City, the salary range is $121,000.00 - $205,000.00 USD.

Actual compensation may vary based on factors including experience, education, certifications, skills, market conditions, internal equity, and geographic location. Compensation and benefits information pertains solely to candidates hired within the United States (local market compensation and benefits will apply for others).

This position is eligible for a short-term incentive called the Short Term Incentive (STI).

At MiniMed, we are committed to supporting the well-being and financial security of our employees. Regular employees working 20 or more hours per week are eligible for a robust benefits package, including health, dental, and vision insurance, as well as access to a Health Savings Account, Healthcare Flexible Spending Account, life insurance, long-term disability leave, and a dependent daycare spending account. In addition, all regular employees enjoy incentive plans, a 401(k) plan with company match, short-term disability coverage, paid time off and holidays, participation in our Employee Stock Purchase Plan, and access to our Employee Assistance Program. Eligible employees may also benefit from our Non-qualified Retirement Plan Supplement and Capital Accumulation Plan, subject to IRS minimum earnings requirements. Please note that “regular employees” refers to those who are not temporary staff, such as interns, and some benefits may not apply to employees in Puerto Rico.

For further details about our comprehensive benefits, we encourage you to visit the link below.

About MiniMed

MiniMed Benefits Overview

MiniMed is a full-stack insulin delivery company dedicated to supporting people living with diabetes through every step of their journey — when and how they need it. For more than 40 years, we’ve been committed to redefining what’s possible: intelligent dosing systems designed for real life, predictive insights that stay a step ahead, and always on support when it’s needed most. At the heart of everything we do is a simple Mission: to make every day a better day for people with diabetes.

Learn more about our business, and our mission here.

jobs.title: Data Analyst - Remote Work
jobs.description:
About the Role

One Call is seeking a detail-oriented and analytical Part-Time Data Analyst to support initiatives across its analytics and operations teams. This role focuses on turning complex data into actionable insights that help inform business decisions and improve operational performance.

You will work with healthcare claims, provider performance, and client outcome data while collaborating with operations, clinical, and IT teams. This part-time position offers a flexible schedule of 20–25 hours per week and is suited to someone who can work independently, manage priorities, and contribute to data-driven healthcare solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Analyze and interpret complex datasets related to healthcare claims, provider performance, and client outcomes.
Develop reports, dashboards, and visualizations to communicate findings and insights to stakeholders.
Collaborate with operations, clinical, and IT teams to define data requirements and support ongoing analytics projects.
Identify trends, variances, and performance indicators to support strategic initiatives.
Assist in maintaining and optimizing data pipelines and databases.
Maintain data quality and integrity while ensuring compliance with privacy standards, including HIPAA.
Prepare ad hoc analyses as requested by leadership.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Healthcare Informatics, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.
At least 2 years of experience in data analysis or business intelligence.
Proficiency in SQL, Excel, and at least one data visualization tool, such as Tableau or Power BI.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently, manage time effectively, and prioritize multiple tasks.
Availability for 20–25 hours per week, with some flexibility during project deadlines.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in healthcare or insurance is preferred.
Familiarity with healthcare claims data or workers’ compensation is a plus.

About One Call

One Call is a provider of specialty healthcare solutions for the workers’ compensation industry. The company connects injured workers with the care they need through technology, data-driven insights, and a service-focused approach. Its mission is to improve health outcomes for injured workers while reducing costs and administrative burdens for clients.

Employment Details and Benefits

Part-time employment.
20–25 hours per week.
Remote work options available.
Competitive hourly compensation.
Opportunity to contribute to work that impacts lives.
Collaborative and inclusive team environment.
Access to learning and development tools.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Agent Harness & Evaluation: Python, TypeScript & LLM Agents | San Jose, CA (On-site) | Up to $350K + Equity
jobs.description:
"Listen to the technology; find out what it's telling you." - Carver Mead, the Caltech professor who taught a generation of engineers how to design a chip.

Sixty years of silicon progress, and the machines still can't tell us where they hurt. A droid in a film gets to whistle indignantly when something is broken. Real hardware just fails a test at 3am and leaves an engineer scrolling waveforms until sunrise.

That is the gap this role sits in. Our client builds AI agents that work on hardware engineering problems - the design, debug and verification grind that eats the schedule of every chip team on earth. The agents are already in production with paying customers. Your job is to make them genuinely good.

This role is based in San Jose, California, five days on-site. Relocation support is available.

WHAT YOU WILL ACTUALLY BE DOING

Breaking the agents on purpose. Finding the failure modes, then building evaluations that measure performance, reliability and efficiency honestly. Not vibes, and not a demo that works once.

Building new agent capability. Tool interfaces, context management, memory, and multi-step or multi-agent orchestration. The harness itself - the thing that decides whether a clever model becomes a useful product.

Reading traces like an investigator. Digging through experiment results for the real bottleneck, and knowing the difference between a genuine improvement and benchmark noise.

Sitting with customers. Hardware engineers and domain experts will describe what is broken in their own language. You translate, build the fix, and own it end to end.

Turning experiments into software. Research that works in a notebook is a starting point, not a deliverable. You make it maintainable, tested and production grade.

THE SCORECARD

Dealbreakers

Real depth across LLM agents, orchestration, tool interfaces, memory, tracing, ML inference and transformer architectures. Systems you have run at scale, with large data and complicated tooling. Recommender systems, LLM gateways and infrastructure plumbing, side projects and straightforward RAG chatbots are not clearing this bar. Agents have to be the day job.
The ability to sit in front of customers, understand what they actually need, and deliver the technical answer yourself. This is scored as a dealbreaker, not a bonus.

Baseline

8 to 15 years as a software engineer, with serious time on large-scale agent systems. The bar is staff-plus.
Time at a rigorous technology company (think Applied Intuition, Palantir, Tesla) or at a serious AI startup (Fireworks, Harvey, strong Y Combinator companies).
A CS, EE or similar degree from a top university.
Production software engineering in Python and TypeScript. Both, properly.
Self-directed and ambitious, with strong ownership, creativity and product judgement.

Nice to have

Experience or interest in electronic design automation (EDA), semiconductor domains, RTL, or hardware-software systems. Not required, but it is the single clearest differentiator in this pipeline.

What will stop you

US citizens and Green Card holders only. No sponsorship and no visa transfer, so O-1, OPT and H-1B are non-starters.
Under a year in your current role is flagged as a trait to avoid.

COMPENSATION

Base: $250,000 to $350,000, with negotiating room for the right person.
Equity: competitive, on top of base.
Location: San Jose, California, five days on-site, relocation support available.

HOW TO APPLY

Apply here, or email keiran@bigwavedigital.com.au with a short note on an agent system you have shipped to production: what you owned across tools, memory and orchestration, and how you knew it was actually working.

If you are close but not an exact match on the scorecard, apply anyway and tell me where you think the gap is.

new_jobs.title: Software Engineer, Agent Harness & Evaluation: Python, TypeScript & LLM Agents | San Jose, CA (On-site) | Up to $350K + Equity
new_jobs.description:
"Listen to the technology; find out what it's telling you." - Carver Mead, the Caltech professor who taught a generation of engineers how to design a chip.

Sixty years of silicon progress, and the machines still can't tell us where they hurt. A droid in a film gets to whistle indignantly when something is broken. Real hardware just fails a test at 3am and leaves an engineer scrolling waveforms until sunrise.

That is the gap this role sits in. Our client builds AI agents that work on hardware engineering problems - the design, debug and verification grind that eats the schedule of every chip team on earth. The agents are already in production with paying customers. Your job is to make them genuinely good.

This role is based in San Jose, California, five days on-site. Relocation support is available.

WHAT YOU WILL ACTUALLY BE DOING

Breaking the agents on purpose. Finding the failure modes, then building evaluations that measure performance, reliability and efficiency honestly. Not vibes, and not a demo that works once.

Building new agent capability. Tool interfaces, context management, memory, and multi-step or multi-agent orchestration. The harness itself - the thing that decides whether a clever model becomes a useful product.

Reading traces like an investigator. Digging through experiment results for the real bottleneck, and knowing the difference between a genuine improvement and benchmark noise.

Sitting with customers. Hardware engineers and domain experts will describe what is broken in their own language. You translate, build the fix, and own it end to end.

Turning experiments into software. Research that works in a notebook is a starting point, not a deliverable. You make it maintainable, tested and production grade.

THE SCORECARD

Dealbreakers

Real depth across LLM agents, orchestration, tool interfaces, memory, tracing, ML inference and transformer architectures. Systems you have run at scale, with large data and complicated tooling. Recommender systems, LLM gateways and infrastructure plumbing, side projects and straightforward RAG chatbots are not clearing this bar. Agents have to be the day job.
The ability to sit in front of customers, understand what they actually need, and deliver the technical answer yourself. This is scored as a dealbreaker, not a bonus.

Baseline

8 to 15 years as a software engineer, with serious time on large-scale agent systems. The bar is staff-plus.
Time at a rigorous technology company (think Applied Intuition, Palantir, Tesla) or at a serious AI startup (Fireworks, Harvey, strong Y Combinator companies).
A CS, EE or similar degree from a top university.
Production software engineering in Python and TypeScript. Both, properly.
Self-directed and ambitious, with strong ownership, creativity and product judgement.

Nice to have

Experience or interest in electronic design automation (EDA), semiconductor domains, RTL, or hardware-software systems. Not required, but it is the single clearest differentiator in this pipeline.

What will stop you

US citizens and Green Card holders only. No sponsorship and no visa transfer, so O-1, OPT and H-1B are non-starters.
Under a year in your current role is flagged as a trait to avoid.

COMPENSATION

Base: $250,000 to $350,000, with negotiating room for the right person.
Equity: competitive, on top of base.
Location: San Jose, California, five days on-site, relocation support available.

HOW TO APPLY

Apply here, or email keiran@bigwavedigital.com.au with a short note on an agent system you have shipped to production: what you owned across tools, memory and orchestration, and how you knew it was actually working.

If you are close but not an exact match on the scorecard, apply anyway and tell me where you think the gap is.
